name: Trans-Late Ancient Relics
focus: Middle Egyptian with a separate reversible ESHB bridge
principles: Do not confuse modern ESHB encoding with historical Egyptian language translation.
Preserve ambiguity and intent rather than forcing one gloss.
Do not auto-promote AI-generated linguistic claims into the trusted lexicon.
Do not persist live camera frames by default.
Expose uncertainty, provenance and review state to learners and reviewers.
Design input/output for text, voice, camera and touch across phone, tablet and desktop.

layers.purpose: Reversible IPA ↔ ESHB with Unicode fallback
Egyptological transliteration, Unicode hieroglyphs, Gardiner/MdC metadata
layers.reversible: partial because historical spelling and sign function are context-sensitive

layers.purpose: Curated trilingual lexicon, ambiguity-aware lexical analysis and conservative grammar templates
Combine deterministic analysis, discourse context, register and optional AI ranking without hiding uncertainty
Live/uploaded relic image analysis with validated image transport and optional multimodal AI
Browser speech recognition/synthesis plus explicitly conventional Egyptological classroom reading
26 lessons, quizzes, progress and voice-assisted examples
Human/AI proposals, unresolved-term queue, reviewer approval and runtime lexicon overlay
Session authentication and role-based access for learner/contributor/reviewer/admin

knowledge_loop.ai_action: draft candidate lexicon proposals when explicitly configured

privacy.camera: permission is requested in the browser and frames are not persisted by the application
privacy.microphone: browser speech APIs are user initiated; backend does not receive raw microphone audio
